floor_history.headline: Honest floor 17 -> 9: the 3 missing insns were cse forwarding the D_80101E60 reload; an aggregate (BLKmode) store of the D_80101E6C/D_80101E70 record flushes cse's memory table in pure C and restores

frontier.hypothesis: The 8-byte record at 0x80101E6C is a real struct-typed global, and declaring it as one in include/code6cac.h reproduces the score-9 bytes without the pointer-alias cast (and lets the extern volatile s32 D_80101E70 cheat at code6cac_b2_post.c:45 be dropped).
frontier.mechanism: Same BLKmode-destination flush of cse's memory table; the cast is only a probe spelling of the same aggregate assignment. Independent evidence for the record: code6cac_b2_post.c:277 passes &D_80101E6C to cdrom_BcdToFrames/cdrom_FramesToBcd as a buffer.
frontier.next_probe: Declare the record type + the global (and, if it holds up at the use sites, SpecialCam as an array of that type), drop both casts, re-run sandbox --disable all and require the score to stay at 9 with identical bytes.

frontier.hypothesis: The entire remaining residual is the schedule position of the pre-jal reload: cc1's sched1 hoists the lh above the two record loads, which removes the load-delay nop AND pushes the copied words out of $a0/$a1.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 ready-list priority - the lh feeds a 3-insn chain (nop/sll/jal-arg) versus the record loads' 1-insn chain, so it wins the hoist. In target the lh is pinned by the anti-dependence on sw a0,%lo(D_80101E6C).
frontier.next_probe: cc1 -da on the sandbox .i, keep the .sched/.greg dumps in tmp/grind/func_80036FD4/s2/, read the ready-list priorities; then try C shapes that shorten the reload's chain to the call or lengthen the record copy's - e.g. hoisting the call argument into its own statement after the copy, or deriving it from the already-live entry pointer.

frontier.hypothesis: If the aggregate copy took GCC's emit_block_move/movstrsi path instead of move_by_pieces it would survive as an opaque memory insn through sched1 and hard-block the lh hoist, which is exactly target's shape.
frontier.mechanism: move_by_pieces expands the 8-byte aligned copy into two transparent SImode moves at expand time, so sched1 can reorder around them; a block-move insn cannot be reordered across.
frontier.next_probe: Measure whether a differently-shaped record (member layout / declared alignment) takes the movstrsi path and whether it changes the schedule WITHOUT changing the emitted load/store shape. Reject any record shape whose only justification is that it schedules well - the layout must be justified from how the bytes at 0x80101E6C are used.
